eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble forecasts from the ECMWF and DWD cluster Munich’s August 18 maximum near 19–21 °C, reflecting strengthening westerly flow that advects cooler maritime air across southern Germany. Persistent stratiform cloud cover and scattered showers further reduce surface insolation, suppressing daytime heating below late-summer climatological norms around 23 °C. Minor differences among the leading market outcomes hinge on exact cloud-break timing, boundary-layer mixing depth, and any localized convective cells that could briefly elevate readings by 1–2 °C. Official observations from Munich Airport will resolve the market once the 24-hour maximum is confirmed.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Japan Meteorological Agency forecasts and ensemble models for August 18 position Tokyo’s daily maximum near 30–31°C under partly cloudy skies with low precipitation odds. This consensus underpins the closely matched market-implied probabilities for those outcomes, reflecting traders’ assessment of urban heat island amplification combined with modest daytime solar heating and light winds. Key differentiating factors include subtle variations in cloud cover that could reduce peak insolation by 1–2°C, boundary-layer humidity influencing surface energy balance, and any late-day sea-breeze shifts capable of moderating temperatures. Historical climatology shows August maxima averaging around 31°C, with ensemble spread and ongoing model updates likely to refine the final recorded value before resolution.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Helsinki Vantaa Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 18 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Helsinki Vantaa Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/fi/vantaa/EFHK.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current forecast consensus from numerical weather prediction models, including runs from the Finnish Meteorological Institute and ECMWF, positions a daily maximum near 20°C in Helsinki on August 18, 2026, under stable high pressure, light southerly flow, and limited cloud cover. This aligns with late-August climatology, where average highs typically fall to 19–20°C amid declining solar insolation and moderating Baltic Sea influence. Recent guidance shows no strong warm advection or radiative cooling signals that would push extremes beyond the narrow 19–21°C envelope, supporting the market’s heavy weighting toward 20°C (54.5%) while assigning lower probabilities to 19°C or 21°C outcomes due to residual uncertainty in boundary-layer mixing. Official observations and updated model ensembles expected later today will refine resolution criteria.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast uncertainty around afternoon convective thunderstorms during the southwest monsoon is the main driver keeping implied probabilities clustered on 32°C and 33°C for Kuala Lumpur’s August 19 maximum. Equatorial solar insolation typically supports peaks near these values under partly cloudy skies, yet variable timing and intensity of monsoon-driven convection—modulated by 70–85% humidity and urban heat-island effects—often produce cloud cover or brief showers that cap readings by 1–2°C. Official guidance from MET Malaysia and global models shows a tight spread consistent with long-term August averages of 31–33°C, with lower odds on 34°C or higher reflecting the low likelihood of fully suppressed rainfall. Traders appear to weigh recent stable conditions against the inherent model divergence on storm development before the daily maximum is reached.
